sections.heading: B — Emergencies, crashes and enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## B — Emergencies, crashes and enforcement stops
Audience: first-time Montana non-commercial Class D applicants studying emergencies, crashes and enforcement stops.
Level: introductory rule retrieval; the ordered handbook section is the coverage basis, without any invented official examination weight. Prerequisites and confusable topics: Vehicle control, warning devices, seatbelts and safe following space.
This is a research handoff. Emergency procedures retain their failure trigger and sequence. Clinical wound assessment, pressure technique and shock intervention are held for current qualified evidence; the dossier retains calling help, immediate-danger movement exceptions and not giving drinks. Generic flare advice never overrides hazardous-load flame-device restrictions.

sections.markdown:
## C — Emergencies, crashes and enforcement stops

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Follow the owner’s maintenance schedule to reduce the chance of a vehicle failure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
If the brakes stop working, pump the pedal several times to try to restore pressure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
If pumping fails, apply a handle-operated parking brake slowly and be ready to release it if the vehicle begins to skid. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
If the parking brake cannot stop the vehicle, shift down and seek a safe place off the road to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not continue driving a vehicle without functioning brakes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
After a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the vehicle moving straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
With a blown tire, release the accelerator, slow gradually and brake lightly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
After a blowout, stop off the road in a safe place whenever possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
If the engine dies while driving, hold the wheel firmly because steering may become harder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
After engine failure, pull off the roadway and expect that braking may require much more pedal pressure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
If headlights suddenly fail, stay calm, release the accelerator and begin braking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
For failed headlights, try the light switch several times and try the high beams. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
If the headlight switch and high beams do not restore lighting, use available flashers, turn signals or fog lamps while pulling off safely as soon as possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A01
If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road and shift promptly to neutral. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A01
With a stuck accelerator, brake with steady pressure and pull off when safe before turning the engine off. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
If the right wheels leave the pavement, release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
After a right-wheel departure, slow first and reenter safely into the right lane using both hands and a small left quarter-turn of the steering wheel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
In the described right-wheel recovery, brake after returning to pavement and remain in the lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
To avoid a collision, a driver may need to stop, turn or accelerate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
Read the owner’s manual for the vehicle’s anti-lock braking procedure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
For a quick stop with anti-lock brakes, press hard and maintain pressure even if the pedal pushes back. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
For a quick stop without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
If non-ABS brakes lock and the vehicle skids, promptly ease off, then reapply as the skid ends, repeating until stopped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A02
Keep both hands firmly on the wheel when making an emergency turn and steer toward the desired path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A02
After an avoidance turn or lane change, remain ready to control the vehicle so the maneuver does not create another collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A02
The handbook describes braking and turning together for vehicles with anti-lock brakes and electronic stability control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A02
Without anti-lock brakes, slow with the brake and then release it before a quick turn; avoid locking the front wheels or turning so sharply that the car plows ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
Acceleration can help avoid a rear or side impact when there is clear room ahead, but slow again after the danger passes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
Use both lap and shoulder belts to reduce injury vulnerability in a collision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A03
For a rear impact, press against the seatback with the head at the restraint and be ready to brake against being pushed into another vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A03
In a side impact, belts remain necessary even with side airbags, and the driver should be ready to steer or brake to avoid a second collision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A03
If a frontal impact is imminent, try to avoid a direct head-on collision by changing the vehicle’s angle when possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A03
Do not stop at a crash unless involved or emergency help has not yet arrived. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A03
Never visit a crash, fire or disaster merely to look, because that can obstruct rescuers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A03
If involved in a crash, stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A03
After hitting a parked vehicle, try to locate its owner. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A03
Notify police when a crash injures or kills someone. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A03
Leaving an injury or fatal crash involving your vehicle before police obtain the needed information is a crime. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0089]

Misconceptions: Brake failure is different from a normal emergency stop; ABS and non-ABS procedures must stay attached to the vehicle’s equipment.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: control the vehicle, stop safely, call help, record and report.
Glossary: Parking brake; tire blowout; anti-lock brakes; electronic stability control; Highway Patrol report; enforcement stop.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle-specific controls and current crash-reporting or move-over applicability require the stated equipment and source conditions; no generic deployment or skid-prevention guarantee is asserted.

sections.heading: C2 — Emergencies, crashes and enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Emergencies, crashes and enforcement stops

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
Stop at or near the crash and move a movable vehicle off the road so it does not obstruct traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes at a crash scene. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Turn wrecked vehicles’ ignitions off and do not smoke near them because spilled fuel may ignite. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
Stay away from downed electrical wires at a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
Use appropriate warning devices to keep other traffic from entering the crash scene. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A02
If someone is injured, ensure police and emergency medical or rescue help have been called, and report any fire. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A02
Do not move an injured person unless a burning vehicle or another immediate danger requires it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A02
Do not give an injured person anything to drink, including water. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A02
Record the names and addresses of people involved, witnesses and injured people. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A02
Exchange driver names, addresses and license numbers, vehicle plates and descriptions, and insurance company and policy details. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A02
The vehicle information exchanged after a crash includes plate number, make, model and year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
Record vehicle damage and provide requested information to police or emergency officials. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
If a parked vehicle’s owner cannot be found after a crash, leave a visible note with contact information and the crash date and time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A02
Immediately notify law enforcement of a crash involving injury, death or property damage of at least 500 dollars. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A02
An injury, death or at least 1,000 dollars of damage to one person’s property requires a Highway Patrol report within ten days. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A02
If injury prevents filing the crash report, another person may file it for the injured driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A02
When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction, yield and, when safe and possible, pull to the right edge and stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A02
With an emergency vehicle using audio and visual signals, non-emergency vehicles must move immediately parallel and as close as possible to the right curb or edge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A02
On a highway posted at 50 miles per hour or more, traffic in the lane directly next to a stationary signaling emergency or police vehicle must travel at least 20 miles per hour below the posted limit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A02
When possible, move to a lane farther from a stationary emergency or police vehicle displaying emergency signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A02
Police emergency signals may include a siren or flashing or rotating red, blue or amber lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A02
The listed authorized-emergency-vehicle signals include a siren or flashing or rotating red or amber lamps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A03
When pulled over, acknowledge the officer by switching on the right turn signal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A03
For an enforcement stop, follow the patrol vehicle’s guidance and pull to the right shoulder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A03
During an enforcement stop, do not stop in the center median or on the opposite side of a two-lane road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A03
Pull as far off the road as possible and choose a well-lit stopping place when available. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A03
During a traffic stop, end phone conversations and switch the radio off. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A03
Remain in the vehicle unless the officer directs you to get out. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A03
The driver and passengers should keep their hands clearly visible to the officer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A03
With tinted windows, the handbook recommends lowering them after stopping on the right shoulder and before the officer makes contact. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0091]
